title: How to Move Subscribers Between Billing Apps Without Double Charging
excerpt: Migrating recurring orders is a scheduling problem with money attached, not an export and an import. Here is the field list, the freeze window and the re authorization flow that keep subscribers from paying twice in one month.
body: Moving subscribers between billing platforms looks like an export and an import. It is really a scheduling problem with money attached. A subscriber billed on the fourteenth who gets imported as a new record billed immediately has now paid twice in one month, and the refund costs more in support time and trust than the migration was supposed to save.

Start from a field list rather than the platform default export. You need email, subscription status, plan and variant, quantity, price, currency, billing interval, next billing date, created date, payment method type, discount code in use, and the shipping address. Two fields are usually missing and always matter: the number of successful charges so far, and any pause or skip already scheduled in the next sixty days. Without them, loyalty tiers break and paused customers get billed.

Freeze the edges of the migration. Close new signups and pause plan changes for the window, then take the final export after the freeze starts. Announce the freeze to the team, not to customers, because a customer who changes plan mid migration becomes a record that exists correctly in neither system. Stagger the work by cohort, oldest first, so problems surface on the smallest possible group instead of the whole book.

Treat the next billing date as a hard requirement and test it on ten subscribers before doing a hundred. Import with billing disabled, verify the date, amount and currency in the new system, then enable billing one cohort at a time. Where possible run a read only overlap for one cycle, so a charge that goes missing can still be found in the old records rather than inferred from a support ticket.

Card details rarely move between platforms, so plan a re authorization flow instead of assuming a silent transfer. Send a short notice before the first charge asking the customer to confirm the payment method, and give a grace window before the subscription pauses. Customers who ignore two emails are not necessarily churning; they are often on a phone that does not autofill. A one tap link outperforms a portal login every time.

Reconcile for two full cycles. Compare charge counts, failed payment rates and active subscriber totals between the two systems on the same date, and investigate anyone who appears twice or not at all. Keep the old system readable for ninety days after cutover, because the questions arrive late and the answers live in the thing you were about to switch off. The DTCwise Subscription and Loyalty category at /category/subscription keeps the current billing app shortlist with pricing, and /tool/recharge covers the day to day side of running recurring orders.
